title: A fresh clone joins the team's board over MCP and the server too, not only the CLI
description:
On a fresh clone `.sober/config.jsonc` is tracked, so `.sober/` exists and `findRoot` succeeds while `project.json` is missing. The CLI catches this (packages/cli/src/board.ts noBoard + adoptBoard). MCP and the server do not:
- MCP `init` says 'already a board here' and never adopts (packages/mcp/src/tools/plan.ts).
- MCP `board`/`decisions` render an empty board silently (loadBoard treats a missing project as null).
- MCP `sync` creates a fresh orphan board branch and merges it with the remote's unrelated history (merge-base → ''), pushing a second root commit and skipping the project check.
- Server `init` route calls initBoard without adoptBoard (packages/server/src/routes.ts).
No data is lost (materialize only writes under .sober/, push is not forced), but the history is polluted and the person is misled.
Fix: MCP openBoard throws NoBoardError (naming `init` as the way to take the team's board) when project.json is missing; MCP `init` and server `init` try adoptBoard first, the way the CLI does. One test each.

brief.approach:
Score 5: three small changes in two packages, but the failure being fixed is a second root commit pushed onto the team's board branch, so the tests matter more than the code.

The CLI already gets this right and is the model for all three changes — read `packages/cli/src/board.ts` first: `noBoard` (line 52) uses `boardTravels` to tell "no board anywhere" from "the team has one and this clone has not taken it", `init` (line 88) tries `adoptBoard` before `initBoard`, and `takeBoard` (line 66) does the same on `sync`. `boardTravels` and `adoptBoard` are already exported from `core`; nothing new is needed there.

**1. `openBoard` in `packages/mcp/src/context.ts` must refuse, not return an empty board.** `findRoot` succeeds on a fresh clone because `.sober/config.jsonc` is tracked, so `.sober/` exists while `project.json` does not — and today `openBoard` hands back `paths`, `loadBoard` treats a missing project as null, and `board` and `decisions` render an empty board in silence. Add the check after the `needsMigration` one: read the project the way `core` does (`readProject`, already exported) and when it is `missing`, throw. `NoBoardError` at line 3 is the right error but its sentence is wrong for this case — it says "there is no board in this repository yet", which is exactly the false thing. Give it the two sentences `noBoard` distinguishes: call `boardTravels(root)`, and when it answers a branch, say the board is on that branch and is not in this clone yet, and that the `init` tool takes it rather than making a second one. When it answers null, keep today's sentence. A refusal here is an answer the model reads and relays (the doc comment on `refusal` in the same file says so), which is why this is a throw and not a silent empty board.

**2. The `init` tool in `packages/mcp/src/tools/plan.ts` (line 79) must adopt first.** Line 90 is `if (findRoot(root) !== null) return text('There is already a board here — nothing changed.')` — on a fresh clone `findRoot` succeeds and the tool says that sentence about a board this clone does not have, and never adopts. Reorder to match the CLI's `init`: after the `isRepo` guard, if the project record is missing, resolve the configured board branch and try `adoptBoard`; on a non-null result return how many records arrived and from which branch, and stop. Only when there is nothing to adopt does it fall through to `initBoard` + `detectSetup` + `createBoardBranch` as it does today. Keep "safe to call twice" true: with a project record present, return the existing sentence unchanged.

**3. The server's `init` route in `packages/server/src/routes.ts:117` calls `initBoard` with no adopt.** Same fix, same order — try `adoptBoard` first when the project record is missing, then `initBoard`. The route's return shape is whatever `initBoard` gives; keep it, and let the adopt path return the same shape so the dashboard needs no change. This node does not touch the dashboard.

**What is deliberately not done here.** MCP `sync` creating an orphan board branch and merging it against unrelated history is named in the node's text as part of the same defect, and fixing (1) fixes it: `sync` goes through `openBoard`, which now refuses before any branch is cut. Add the test for it, but do not write a second guard inside the sync tool — one refusal in one place is the point.

**Tests, one per surface, each proving the fresh-clone case rather than the happy path.** Build the fixture the way `test/integration/sync.test.ts` already builds two clones of one bare remote (its header calls it M2's gate in miniature) — that file has the exact setup for "a second clone with a board on the remote and no `project.json` locally". 
- MCP: in `test/integration/mcp.test.ts`, on such a clone, `board` returns the refusal naming the branch instead of an empty board, and `sync` does the same rather than pushing a second root commit. Assert the remote's board branch still has exactly one root commit afterwards — `git rev-list --max-parents=0 <branch> | wc -l` — because that is the damage, and a test that only checks the message would pass while the history is polluted.
- MCP `init` on that clone adopts: it returns the record count and the branch, and the local board branch now points at the remote's commit rather than a new orphan.
- Server: in `test/integration/wire.test.ts` or beside the existing server route tests, the `init` route on that clone adopts rather than writing a second project record.

Nothing else changes: no new `core` export, no schema change, no CLI edit — the CLI is already correct and is the reference, not the target.

acceptance.proves: on a fresh clone whose board lives on the remote, the MCP tools refuse with the sentence naming the branch instead of rendering an empty board, and sync no longer cuts an orphan branch
the server's init route adopts the team's board instead of writing a second project record, and every other route still behaves

acceptance.run: pnpm vitest run --project integration test/integration/sync.test.ts test/integration/cli.test.ts
acceptance.proves: the CLI's own adopt path — the reference this node copies — is unchanged, and two clones of one remote still sync as they did

acceptance.run: git grep -q 'boardTravels' -- packages/mcp/src/context.ts && git grep -q 'adoptBoard' -- packages/mcp/src/tools/plan.ts packages/server/src/routes.ts
acceptance.proves: all three surfaces now use the same two core functions the CLI uses, rather than each inventing its own fresh-clone detection
only the two surfaces and their tests changed — core gained no export, the schema did not move, and the CLI was left exactly as it is
the reordered init paths and the widened refusal compile in both packages
